intro: Match each development to whether it shows continuity or change — and what changed.

left.label: 1640 ruling — unfree labor status, no racial split yet

right.label: Continuity — servitude of some kind already existed at the colony's founding
Change — status begins to split by race; one sentence "has an end," one does not
Change — the turning point that accelerates the shift to permanent, race-based slavery
Continuity — representative self-government, present from the colonies' founding
Change — the same idea restated, but this document asks who self-government actually included

rationale.a: The 1640 ruling shows unfree labor already existed — the continuity is that servitude of some kind was present from the start.
rationale.b: By 1662 and 1669, the rulings stop matching by offense and start splitting by race — the change is underway before 1676.
rationale.c: Bacon's Rebellion, 1676, is the accelerant — after it, the split hardens into a permanent, race-based system.
rationale.d: The Fundamental Orders, 1639, show representative self-government was already part of the colonies' founding idea — the continuity that carries to Document 18.
rationale.e: Blackstone restates the same self-government idea, but Document 18 #5 asks who it actually meant it for — the same principle, a changed (or exposed) scope.
